inicio.titulo: Browser agents: test your site the way the agent sees it
inicio.lead: Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, and the agent side that consumes WebMCP, all running against a local page. You write the contract for each task, see where the screen fails, and walk away with a battery that an agent runs against your site and saves to a file.
inicio.capa_alt: A dark monitor with an open browser and, next to it, an industrial humanoid robot operating the keyboard.
inicio.aulas_sub: From the agent map to your site's battery: Playwright MCP, DevTools MCP, the side that consumes WebMCP, the contract, the test in a file, where the screen fails, and the battery.

itens: Web devs or QA who edit HTML and JavaScript and run commands in the terminal.
Anyone who wants to know whether a browser agent can use their own site, before a customer finds out.
Anyone who has already done course 0 (or knows how to read the accessibility tree) and wants to test for real.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Connect Playwright MCP and Chrome DevTools MCP to Claude Code or Codex and see what they see.
See how an agent discovers and calls a page's WebMCP tools, and what happens without the API.
Write a task contract: goal, limits, proof, and stop.
Run a battery of tasks against your site, with the result in a file and the agent stopping where it should.

blocos.t: Where this course fits in the WebMCP Program
itens: Before: 0 · basics, 1 · MCP server, 2 · WebMCP on the page. After: 4 · security, 5 · expert.
Before you start: Node 20.19+, 22.12+ or 23+, git, and a Linux or macOS terminal (WSL on Windows). Claude Code or Codex only for the optional step in lesson 6.
The kit, the example site, and the script messages are in Portuguese in all versions of the course; the commands are the same.
